title: Routing header canonicalization mutated stop-sequences causing customer JSON eval failures
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden JSON parsing failures in automated evals after the 1.22 routing change. Root cause traced to a header-canonicalization pass in the routing/fallback layer that normalized incoming stop-sequence headers and, in some cases, mutated multi-byte or whitespace-sensitive stop markers. The mutated stop sequences were either (a) stripped/truncated or (b) converted to a different whitespace character, which allowed model output to include trailing tokens that broke downstream JSON-based evaluators. This ticket tracks investigation, immediate customer mitigation, and a patch to preserve exact stop-sequence semantics across routing/fallback and model-variant translations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a request with X-Redwood-StopSeq header set to a multi-token sequence containing non-breaking spaces (e.g., '\u00A0') or explicit newline anchors ("""---END---""").
2) Route the request through configured header-based routing that triggers fallback policy to a compatible model variant (hosted -> dedicated or to lower-cost variant).
3) Observe that the returned text contains the original stop marker partially present or replaced (e.g., NBSP -> regular space) and the eval harness fails JSON.parse on output.
4) Re-run with header-canonicalization disabled in routing layer: output matches expected stop-sequence behavior and eval passes.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-06: Reproduced against customer-supplied prompt and stop-sequence using internal replay infra (replay-id: rbw-replay-20260306-01).

Routing change introduced in commit runtime-routing#b12a7 which applied Unicode normalization and whitespace trimming for headers to unify legacy clients. That transform removed NBSP and trimmed trailing \n, breaking literal stop tokens used by several customers.

Fallback path to model-variant 'gptx-async-v2-quant' uses an older termination sequence sanitizer that expects ASCII-only stop markers; combined effect caused double-normalization and dropped the last token in multi-token stop sequences.
KV-cache and batching do not appear to be the proximate cause; logs show tokenization and termination checks on server-side observed the mutated sequence before generating completion tokens.
Affected customers identified: ACME Finance (hosted), NovusHealth (dedicated private pool), and BetaRetail (private), with varying failure rates (10-40% of eval runs).
action_items: A1: Roll back header-canonicalization transform in routing layer for stop-related headers (owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-03-12).
A2: Add strict pass-through for X-Redwood-StopSeq and stop_seq request fields; add validation to detect multi-byte/whitespace-sensitive sequences (owner: Runtime Routing team, ETA: 2026-03-14).
A3: Patch fallback translator to avoid a second normalization pass when stop markers are present (owner: Runtime team, ETA: 2026-03-16).
A4: Deploy canary to 10% of traffic with additional telemetry to detect mutated sequences (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-13).
A5: Provide mitigation checklist and temporary customer workarounds to support (owner: Solutions Eng, ETA: 2026-03-09).
A6: Add unit + integration tests covering NBSP, zero-width spaces, multiline and explicit anchor stop tokens across hosted/dedicated/private routing permutations (owner: QA, ETA: 2026-03-18).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Hotfix (2026-03-12) - revert header canonicalization for X-Redwood-StopSeq only and enable feature-flagged strict pass-through.
Phase 1: Canary (2026-03-13) - enable on 10% of routing traffic, monitor eval pass rate, token-level diffs, and p50/p95 latency.
Phase 2: Full deploy (2026-03-14 to 2026-03-16) - roll to 100% after canary stability and sign-off from customer success for impacted customers.
Phase 3: Hardening (by 2026-03-18) - backfill tests, add parsing telemetry to console, and include explicit migration notes in release notes for runtime-1.22.
